body: Gabby Williams has put Golden State back in front! The French star has shown nerves of steel, sinking four straight free throws in the space of a minute to turn a three-point deficit into a one-point lead.

It’s been a frantic stretch, with turnovers, blocked shots and missed opportunities at both ends. Howard denied Kaila Charles at the rim, Reese intercepted a Williams pass, while Gray missed a chance to restore Atlanta’s advantage with a layup.
But Williams grabbed the defensive rebound, drew a foul from Reese (her fourth) and coolly deposited both free throws to send Chase Center into a frenzy.
After scoring 16 points in the second quarter to rescue Golden State from a dreadful start, Williams is delivering again when it matters most.

articles.title: Scottish Premiership: Rangers miss chance to go top after pulsating draw with Dundee
articles.summary: Jones equaliser denies Rangers victory. Kilmarnock move off the bottom with 3-2 win. Rangers passed up the chance to go top of the Premiership in a pulsating 2-2 draw against Dundee at Dens Park.
body: Derek McInnes’s side came out re-energised for the second half and took the lead on the hour with midfielder Nico Raskin’s long-range drive but in the 68th minute midfielder Callum Jones took advantage of Gers slackness to level. Dundee were well worth a point with Rangers moving one point behind leaders Celtic, who can increase their lead at home to Hearts on Sunday.

Greg Kiltie scored twice to lift Kilmarnock off the bottom with a 3-2 home victory over Motherwell. Kiltie struck first and last as Neil McCann’s side inflicted a fifth consecutive defeat on the Steelmen, who join Killie in the bottom three, one point above bottom-placed Hibernian.

Motherwell had a dominant spell after recovering from Kiltie’s second-minute opener and goals from Alex Lowry and Seb Palmer-Houlden turned the game on its head. But Tyreece John-Jules soon equalised and Motherwell were cut open before Kiltie knocked home a 69th-minute winner.

articles.summary: Lamine Yamal opens scoring in ninth straight win. Luis Díaz hat-trick helps Bayern thump RB Leipzig 6-1. body: Lamine Yamal lit the fuse with a dazzling opener before Rodri, Gabriel Jesus, Eric García and the substitute Dani Olmo joined the party, while Valentín Gómez and Ez Abde replied ⁠for Betis, who played much of the second half with 10 men after Facundo Bernal was sent off for headbutting Lamine Yamal.

Lamine Yamal opened the scoring in the 10th minute in familiar style, gliding in from the right before whipping a left-footed strike from the edge of the box into the top corner. Betis levelled in the 27th when Pablo Fornals collected a rebound on the right and clipped a cross into the middle for Gómez, who rose highest to head past goalkeeper Joan García.

Barcelona reclaimed the lead on 41 minutes when ‌the Spain captain Rodri powered in a header from Fermín López’s corner. Betis thought they had equalised three minutes later through Gio Lo Celso’s spectacular swivelling volley from outside the box, but the effort was ruled out after Cucho ​Hernández was adjudged to have handled.
Jesus had a goal disallowed for offside shortly after the break but was not kept waiting long. In the 51st, Lamine Yamal darted down the right and squared for the Brazilian to finish neatly.

articles.title: West Ham unstoppable, Norwich in trouble - Aaron McLean's EFL takeaways
articles.summary: BBC Final Score pundit Aaron McLean looks at the weekend's talking points in the EFL, including West Ham win over in-form Swansea City and Norwich City's woes.
body: Former Peterborough United and Hull City striker - and Final Score pundit - Aaron McLean gives his five takeaways following Saturday's action in the Championship, League One and League Two.

West Ham won their fixture with Swansea City in the Championship, thanks to Divine Mukasa's goal, and have moved to within a point of the Welsh club at the top of the table. They've scored a remarkable 30 goals in their 11 league games.
McLean: "I think it was a huge win for West Ham. Take nothing away from Swansea and I think the start they've had has been incredible, but today was always going to be a real test for them.
"After the demolition of Lincoln in midweek, it was important West Ham backed that up with three points to close the gap to just one point behind Swansea and they did that.

But Jones then caught Dan Neil dwelling on the ball and nicked it off the Rangers captain to slot home the Dundee equaliser.

articles.title: Champions Cup: Munster beat Racing on day of Foley tributes as Saracens, Bath lose
articles.summary: A decade to the day since the rugby world learned of head coach Anthony Foley’s death at the age of 42, Munster marked the poignant anniversary with a stirring 33-25 Champions Cup victory over Racing 92.
body: The night of Friday October 16, 2016 saw Foley pass away in his sleep the night before Munster were due to face Racing in Paris, with their fixture 10 years on staged at Páirc Uí Chaoimh in Cork.

Munster crossed for five tries in a hard-fought contest, with No 8 Brian Gleeson, wearing 24 as Foley's retired No 8 was once again taken out of circulation, joined on the scoresheet by wing Shay McCarthy, lock Tadhg Beirne, replacement Fineen Wycherley and scrum-half Craig Casey.

Racing responded with three tries of their own through wing Wilfried Hulleu, replacement scrum-half Maxime Machenaud and full-back Geronimo Prisciantelli, denying Munster a bonus-point victory. Under the tournament's new rules, teams must score at least three more tries than their opponents to secure the full five points.

The match came a day after the shocking death of Lions second row Hyron Andrews in France ahead of a Champions Cup fixture in La Rochelle. Emotional tributes were paid to both Andrews and Foley before kick-off.

articles.title: Kartal hails mentality after 'dream come true' run to Wuhan Open final
articles.summary: Britain's Sonay Kartal says making her maiden WTA 1000 final at the Wuhan Open is a "dream come true," adding that the mental side of sport is "one of my strongest assets."
body: Kartal became only the second British woman, after Johanna Konta (Beijing 2016, Miami 2017, Rome 2019), to reach a WTA 1000 final with a stunning 7-6 (11-9) 7-6 (7-5) victory over Jelena Ostapenko.

The 24-year-old, playing in only her third tournament since returning from a back injury, saved multiple set points to punish Ostapenko, despite the Latvian hitting an astonishing 50 winners in the match.
Kartal will take on Maja Chwalinska in Sunday's final, live on Sky Sports Tennis from 11.30am, after the French Open finalist upset fellow Pole and former world No 1 Iga Swiatek 7-5 6-1.
"I've been shooting to get this far in one of these events for a very long time and to be able to do it this fast after so long out, is special.
